# Xin API 🚀

[English](https://github.com/GripAIcn/Xin-api/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Chinese

---

## ✨ Project Overview

Xin API is a high-performance large language model (LLM) gateway service that seamlessly supports mainstream LLMs such as OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, and Gemini. It provides unified API access, channel routing, billing and settlement, and observability.

### Core Features

- **🎯 Unified API access**: The data plane provides three inbound protocol endpoints, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`, all routed uniformly to upstream providers
- **🔀 Smart distribution**: Route selection uses "priority + weighted round-robin among equal priority". Failed requests are retried automatically, and already-failed channels are excluded
- **🛡️ Circuit breaker protection**: Redis-based distributed passive circuit breaking. After consecutive failures reach a threshold, the channel is isolated automatically and probed for recovery at the recovery interval
- **⚡ Rate limiting (reserved)**: A Redis-based token bucket rate-limiting middleware is implemented but not yet attached to the data plane in the current version, so `rpm_limit` / `tpm_limit` are not yet in effect
- **👥 Unified channel management**: Centrally manage upstream provider channels and configure weights, priorities, and statuses. Channel-level "model management" supports add/edit/delete, enable/disable, and pulling models from upstream
- **🗂️ Model management**: Aggregates available models across channels by logical model name, with batch add, edit, and enable/disable across channels
- **🔁 Model name mapping**: Registers the real upstream model name for each "channel × external model name" pair. Requests are rewritten to the upstream name when forwarded, and responses are rewritten back to the external name
- **🧩 Multi-protocol adaptation**: Inbound supports OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, and native Gemini protocols. Outbound adapts to OpenAI / DeepSeek / Anthropic / Gemini according to the channel's provider
- **💰 Billing and settlement**: Price plans support USD / CNY pricing, converted to CNY at the configured exchange rate for settlement. Balance changes and exchange-rate snapshots are recorded
- **🔑 API Key management**: Flexible API key distribution and revocation

---

Neuro OJ (NOJ) is an independent community project with no official relationship to CCF, LMCC, IOAI, or NOAI.

> [!CAUTION]
> Neuro OJ
> is still in development and has not undergone formal production validation. Do not use it to judge any official competition.

## Introduction

NOJ provides a complete workflow from "register → solve → submit → evaluate". It can be used for LMCC exam preparation and mock training, AI certification and selection, course practical training, and model evaluation competitions.

The main difference from traditional OJs is that problems are scored by an evaluator that calls functions implemented by the user, rather than only comparing standard input and output (stdin/stdout). This approach is better suited to evaluating LLM applications and AI engineering ability.

## Core Features

- **Function-call-based evaluation**: The evaluator drives tests and customizes scoring logic, covering objective questions, code problems, LLM engineering problems, and artifact submission problems.
- **Dual-container security sandbox**: User code and evaluation code run isolated in separate Docker containers. The Solution has networking disabled, while the Evaluator may access the network as configured per problem and is subject to resource limits.
- **Full competitions and community**: Problem filtering, submission records, leaderboards, competitions, real-time evaluation status, community interaction, and RBAC permission management.
- **LLM call gateway**: Unified management of providers, access credentials, rate limiting, and usage auditing.

## Quick Start

Production environments use single-host Docker Compose deployment. Download the `noj-cli` binary from Releases and verify it, then use it to complete the installation. It is recommended to specify `--ref` with a version matching the binary (binaries 0.10.4 and earlier must specify it explicitly):

```bash
VERSION=v0.10.6   # Replace with the target Release tag (see the Releases page)
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/Neuro-OJ/neuro-oj/releases/download/$VERSION/noj-cli-linux-amd64"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/Neuro-OJ/neuro-oj/releases/download/$VERSION/noj-cli-linux-amd64.sha256"
sha256sum -c noj-cli-linux-amd64.sha256
chmod +x noj-cli-linux-amd64
./noj-cli-linux-amd64 install --dir /opt/neuro-oj --ref "$VERSION"
```

SkyAerope/TOTP-Generator-Web.body:
# TOTP Generator

This project is a JavaScript-based web tool that provides a simple and practical interface, allowing users to enter a key (Key) and generate TOTP passwords related to the current time directly on the webpage.

## Deployment

### Server Hosting
Clone all files in the project folder into the root directory of your web server, or host it using any static website hosting service (such as GitHub Pages, Vercel, Netlify, etc.).

### Local Preview

You can open the `index.html` file locally to preview the website.

## Usage Workflow

1. **Save the key when setting up two-factor authentication (2FA)**: When setting up an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator, choose to enter the key manually instead of scanning the QR code. The website will display the 2FA key; save it in a secure place.

2. **Enter the key to get a TOTP**:
   - Open the deployed TOTP generator website.
   - Enter your 2FA key in the input box.
   - The website will generate a short-lived TOTP password based on the current time and the key you entered.
   - Click the generated TOTP password card to copy the password, for use when verification is needed.

## What is TOTP?

TOTP (Time-Based One-Time Password) is a time-based one-time password algorithm used to strengthen authentication security. It is one of the common two-factor authentication (2FA) methods.

Common TOTP apps include **Google Authenticator**, **Authy**, and **Microsoft Authenticator**, among other authentication apps. These apps provide user-friendly interfaces and automatic TOTP password generation.

Typically, users associate a TOTP key with their accounts, such as email, social media, cloud services, and so on. When a user logs in, the system asks the user to enter the TOTP password for the current time to verify identity.

The basic principle of TOTP is to generate a short-lived password based on the current time and a pre-shared key. This password is only valid within a specific time window and becomes invalid once that window has passed.

The process for generating a TOTP password is as follows:
1. The user enters the key (Key) in a device or application.
2. Using a hash algorithm (typically HMAC-SHA1, HMAC-SHA256, etc.) and the key, compute over the current timestamp.
3. Based on the time step length specified by the algorithm (typically 30 seconds), calculate the password for the time step containing the current time.
4. Format the password, typically as 6 digits, and provide it to the user.
5. The password becomes invalid after the next time step, and a new password must be generated.

## Notes

- Make sure the key is kept secure and not disclosed to others.
- When using the TOTP passwords generated by this tool, make sure the time is accurately synchronized; otherwise the generated passwords may be invalid.
- For some temporary accounts, you may choose to save the key in a secure place and then use this tool to get the TOTP each time. Of course, this approach carries significant risk.

## 💻 Problem Description

On HyperOS 3.0 (Android 16)+, the system app Clipboard & Phrases V4.7.7 blocks third-party input methods (such as WeChat Input) from accessing clipboard history data, so third-party input methods cannot use the system clipboard feature.
Built-in official input methods (Sogou Xiaomi custom edition, iFlytek Xiaomi custom edition, Baidu Xiaomi custom edition, Xiaomi Xiaoai input method) are not affected.

## ✏ Supported Input Methods

 ✍️ Testing was done on the versions above. In theory it is compatible with all versions. For perfect operation, please turn off the gesture hint line. Problems caused by the gesture hint line may not be addressed in the future (too troublesome, I am planning to give up on it)!

### 🌡️ Requirements

- Rooted Xiaomi / Redmi phone, HyperOS 3.0+
- Clipboard and Phrases V4.7.7+
- **The LSPosed framework must support the new libxposed module API (API 102)**, for example Vector v2.2 or above
  - The current framework's API version is shown below "Activated" on the LSPosed Manager home page
  - This module is developed on the new API and is not compatible with the old `de.robv.android.xposed`

1. Enable this module in LSPosed
2. Check the scope:
   - **Clipboard and Phrases** (`com.miui.phrase`): required for the clipboard fix

3. After installation, restart the phone, otherwise it will not take effect

## 💕 Special Notes

- This module only modifies the clipboard and phrases verification logic and does not affect data content, so feel free to use it.
- If your system clipboard works normally, please do not install this module!

riverscn/singbox-confgen.body:
# sing-box Config Generator

**Enter your nodes, and DNS, IPv6 and routing are configured according to best practices.**

**Online: <https://sing-box-confgen.riverleaf.dev>**

When a sing-box configuration feels off, the problem is usually not the nodes but things you can't see. This generator tests each of these pitfalls and provides a countermeasure for it. You only need to enter your nodes to get a complete `config.json`, which you can import into SFM, SFI, SFA, or the command-line version to use.

## What It Solves

| Symptom | Cause | Approach here |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic sites resolve to overseas addresses, or blocked domains won't open | DNS doesn't follow routing: domestic domains are queried through overseas DNS, and blocked domains get polluted addresses | Direct connections use local DNS; proxied connections query remote DNS through the proxy; for uncertain domains, both are queried, and the domain connects directly only if the answer is a domestic IP ([DNS policy](https://github.com/riverscn/singbox-confgen/blob/HEAD/DESIGN.md#2-dns-策略)) |
| Some connections bypass the proxy or fail to connect after enabling it | Apps prefer IPv6, but the proxy server has no IPv6, or IPv6 doesn't go through sing-box at all | Proxied traffic only gets A records, with IPv6 hints in HTTPS/SVCB records removed as well; when the local machine has no IPv6, direct connections cleanly fall back to IPv4 ([IPv6 policy](https://github.com/riverscn/singbox-confgen/blob/HEAD/DESIGN.md#3-ipv6-策略)) |
| Sites frequently ask for verification or trigger risk controls | Exit IP drifts between IPv4 and IPv6 and across different servers | Proxied traffic always exits from the same server and the same IPv4 address |
| After switching nodes, some things still use the old route | DNS and rule-set downloads each have their own egress | Proxied traffic, remote DNS, and rule-set downloads share a single `proxy` outbound, so they switch together when you change nodes ([proxy group](https://github.com/riverscn/singbox-confgen/blob/HEAD/DESIGN.md#6-代理组)) |
| With global mode on, your home NAS and company intranet become unreachable | LAN and intranet traffic is also sent through the proxy | LAN traffic connects directly in every mode; outside, the built-in Tailscale connects back to the tailnet, and split DNS resolves intranet addresses ([Tailscale](https://github.com/riverscn/singbox-confgen/blob/HEAD/DESIGN.md#4-tailscale)) |

```bash
npm install -g pzero-operator
operator
```

```bash
operator                          # interactive TUI
operator -p "write tests"         # one-off request, no TUI
operator --continue                # continue the last session
operator --resume                  # pick a session from the list
operator --list-models             # see everything that's available
```
